_meta.indication: Add-on maintenance treatment of patients with severe asthma aged 18 years and older with an eosinophilic phenotype

pivotal_trials.population: Patients 12-75 years of age with eosinophilic asthma, blood eosinophil count ≥ 400 cells/µL, and ≥1 exacerbation in the past 12 months
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Frequency of clinical asthma exacerbations over 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Exacerbation rate ratio 0.50 (95% CI 0.37, 0.67); p<0.0001 (50% reduction vs placebo)

pivotal_trials.population: Patients 12-75 years of age with eosinophilic asthma, blood eosinophil count ≥ 400 cells/µL, and ≥1 exacerbation in the past 12 months
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Frequency of clinical asthma exacerbations over 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Exacerbation rate ratio 0.41 (95% CI 0.28, 0.59); p<0.0001 (59% reduction vs placebo)

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction (≥2%) was oropharyngeal pain (2.6% vs 2.2% placebo). Most serious: anaphylaxis (0.3% of patients; 3 subjects vs 0 placebo) and malignancy (0.6% vs 0.3% placebo).
target_moa: Reslizumab is an interleukin-5 antagonist monoclonal antibody (IgG4 kappa) that binds human IL-5, preventing it from binding the IL-5 receptor alpha chain on eosinophils; neutralization of IL-5 reduces production and survival of eosinophils

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS — anaphylaxis occurred with CINQAIR infusion in 0.3% of patients in placebo-controlled studies; discontinue immediately if anaphylaxis occurs

rems.type: A REMS was determined not necessary; risk mitigation beyond professional labeling not warranted

advisory_committee.vote: PADAC met December 9, 2015; voted 11 Yes / 3 No for approval in adults 18 years and older, and 14 Yes / 0 No against approval (14 No) in pediatrics 12 to 17 years

summary.text: BLA 761033 was submitted by Teva under section 351(a) of the PHS Act, received March 30, 2015, and reviewed under a standard PDUFA timeline (PDUFA goal date March 29-30, 2016). It was a first-cycle approval supported by two pivotal 52-week exacerbation trials (3082 and 3083) plus a lung-function trial (3081); a Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee met December 9, 2015 and voted to support approval in adults but not in adolescents. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority review designation is stated for this application.

citations.quote: Please refer to your Biologics License Application (BLA) dated March 29, 2015, received March 30, 2015, submitted under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for Cinqair (reslizumab).

NDA/BLA #	BLA 761033
Supplement #	Original #1 (ages 18 years and older) (b) (4)
Applicant	Teva Pharmaceuticals
Date of Submission	March 29, 2015
PDUFA Goal Date	March 29, 2016

Two identically-designed concurrently-conducted studies, 37082/3082 (referred to as 3082) and 37082/3083 (referred to as 3083), showed that reslizumab provided statistically significant benefit over placebo with regard to the primary endpoint, frequency of asthma exacerbations during 52 weeks of treatment period. Reslizumab reduced the annual rate of exacerbations by 50% and 59% relative to placeb

A meeting of the Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) was held on December 9, 2015, to discuss this application. Issues for discussion on the efficacy side were the target patient population likely to benefit with reslizumab, adequacy of dose ranging data, adequacy of data in patients 12 to 17 years of age, and adequacy of data in various ethnic subgroups, particularly US population,
